result:
All six deliverables are done. Everything ran in the foreground; nothing is backgrounded and no watcher is armed.

## How I reproduced it — `git version 2.55.0`

Reused `~/piers/joinall-bus` (PID 2519792, port 8093) after scry-confirming its source: `lib/git-protocol.hoon` 14,515 bytes and `app/urgit.hoon` 366,492 bytes, byte-identical to the working tree at `f1fcb95`.

- **Raw HTTP**, 4-byte `0000` body → `HTTP/1.1 400 upload-pack request has no wants`. Same with `Git-Protocol: version=2`. The brief predicted `invalid upload-pack request`; the real message comes from the want check at `urgit.hoon:7872`, not the parse check. A flush-only body parses — it parses to nothing.
- **v0 clone**, `http.postBuffer=1024` on `gz1` → 4-byte POST, 400, exit 128.
- **v2**: `postBuffer=1024` aborts inside git (`BUG: remote-curl.c:1533`). Bisected the floor — **65,524** is the smallest usable value; 65,523 and below abort. Worked around by using 65,536 and a repository whose request exceeds it (`pb1`, 2,000 refs) → 4-byte POST, 400, exit 128.
- **v0 and v2 do not differ.** Same body, same route, same 400, same message. The difference is client-side only.
- **At default settings, no `-c` flag**: built `big1`, 22,001 refs in a star topology → probe sent, exit 128 (v0) / 141 (v2).

## Naming choice

**Took the rename.** `receive-probe` → `flush-only-body`, one arm called from both handlers. The arm never knew anything about `receive-pack` — it decodes one packet, tests for `%flush`, tests the remainder for length zero. Its body is unchanged; only the name and comment moved. A second arm would have left two copies of the same three lines.

## D3 semantics

I ran the real `/usr/libexec/git-core/git-http-backend` as a CGI program with a 4-byte body. It writes **no `Status:` header**, so the server returns **200**, `application/x-git-upload-pack-result`, zero-length body — identical on v0 and v2. Three cases reach the arm: the `probe_rpc` probe; a v0 client that wants nothing (bare flush is the v0 want-list terminator); a v2 body naming no command. 200-with-empty-body is correct for all three.

One caution I recorded: stock also returns 200 for `0000GARBAGE` and for garbage, because it writes headers before starting `upload-pack`. That is CGI ordering, not a ruling — so urgit's 400 for malformed bodies rests on D4, not on stock git.

I could not make git 2.55.0 emit a non-probe bare flush over Smart HTTP: an up-to-date v0 fetch sends **no POST at all**, and an up-to-date v2 fetch sends only a 138-byte `ls-refs`.

## D4 — fail closed

I reinstalled the **pre-fix desk** on the same ship, took the whole matrix, then reinstalled the fix and took it again. Every 400 row is byte-identical on both sides, message included: `0000GARBAGE` → 400, empty → 400, garbage → 400. Only the flush-only rows changed, 400 → 200. Gzipped flush → 200 (proves ordering after `decoded-body`); lying about gzip → 400; `content-encoding: br` → 415. Private repo unauthenticated → **403**, wrong token → 403, correct token → 200; unknown repo → 404; GET → 405.

## D5 — evidence

- **`big1`, 22,001 refs, default settings, no `-c` flag**: probe sent, exit 0, 22,003 objects, hash matches source, `fsck --full` clean — on **both** v0 and v2. The same two clones exit 128/141 pre-fix. The ~21,000-ref case is done, not skipped.
- Forced-probe clones on `pb1` (v0 and v2) and `gz1` (v0): all exit 0, hashes match.
- Regression clones at default settings reproduce `GZIP-REQUEST.md` §5a **byte for byte** — 5,142 / 5,218 / 1,506 / 1,579 / 936 / 1,023 — with every recorded hash.
- **Push still works**: 9,768,379 bytes over the probe (exit 0), 5,271,415 bytes / 22,001 refs over the probe (exit 0), 61,764 bytes / 201 refs under it (exit 0, the same size §1e recorded). Clone-back of the pushed repo gives 1,437 objects and a hash identical to the source working tree.
- **All 19 conformance vectors** match `GZIP-REQUEST.md` §5c.

Final installed state scry-confirmed: 14,651 bytes with `flush-only-body` at 6,336 and no `receive-probe`; app at 367,041 bytes.

## Left undone

`pb1` clones take 85 s against 3.3 s for a same-size star repository — the cost tracks graph depth, not ref count. Recorded so the numbers are not misread; not chased, as the brief directs. The exact default-settings ref threshold (~20,972) is calculated, not bisected. No client other than git 2.55.0 was tested.

Two commits on `feat/progress-and-joinall`: `fa1defd` (fix) and `846a6c2` (report). Not pushed.
